required_parts.name: Drain bolt gasket
required_parts.purpose: New gasket on every drain bolt.

critical_stop_conditions: Oil level not dropping or no oil at the pressure check: stop the engine at once.

steps.instruction: Check the engine oil level every race (about 2.5 hours). Change the engine oil after break-in, then every third race (about 7.5 hours). Write down the date and hours.

steps.instruction: Put the bike upright on level ground on a stand.

steps.instruction: Start the engine, let it warm up for several minutes, then stop it and wait about 5 minutes. The engine stops by itself after 7 minutes at idle: if it does, push the start switch to restart it.

steps.instruction: Refit the oil filler cap.

steps.instruction: With the bike upright, start the engine, let it warm up for 2 to 3 minutes, stop it and wait about 1 minute.

steps.instruction: Read the oil check window: the level must sit between the minimum and maximum marks. Below the minimum mark: add the same oil.
steps.title: Read the level

steps.instruction: Slightly loosen the oil pressure check bolt. Never start the engine with it removed: oil will spout out.

branches.condition: Stop the engine at once so it cannot seize; have the oil passages and pump checked and record it.

steps.instruction: Look round the drain bolt, the filter cover and the filler cap for leaks.
steps.title: Check for leaks

steps.instruction: Write down the date, hours, oil used, amount.

title: Change the engine oil and oil filter
entry_state: Engine cool enough to handle, bike upright on a stand on level ground.
exit_state: Fresh oil at the correct level, new filter fitted, oil pressure confirmed, no leaks, recorded.
completeness: Covers warming, draining, filter replacement, refilling, level check and oil pressure check.

required_parts.name: Engine oil
required_parts.purpose: SAE 10W-40, 10W-50, 15W-40, 20W-40 or 20W-50 four-stroke oil rated API SG or higher and JASO MA (Yamalube is the named brand).

required_parts.name: Drain bolt gaskets
required_parts.purpose: New gasket on every drain bolt.

required_parts.name: Oil filler cap O-ring
required_parts.purpose: New O-ring.

required_parts.name: Oil filter element
required_parts.purpose: New filter.

required_parts.name: Oil filter element cover O-ring
required_parts.purpose: New O-ring.

critical_stop_conditions: Oil level not dropping or no oil at the pressure check: stop the engine at once.
Do not rev the engine during the pressure check.

steps.instruction: Check the engine oil level every race (about 2.5 hours). Change the engine oil after break-in, then every third race (about 7.5 hours). Replace the oil filter element after break-in, then every fifth race (about 12.5 hours). Write down the date and hours.
steps.title: Record the starting point

steps.instruction: Put the bike upright on level ground on a stand.
steps.title: Stand the bike upright

steps.instruction: Start the engine, let it warm up for several minutes, then turn it off.
steps.title: Warm the engine

steps.instruction: Put a drain pan under the engine oil drain bolts.
steps.title: Place a drain pan

steps.instruction: Remove the oil filler cap with its O-ring.
steps.title: Remove the filler cap

steps.instruction: Remove the engine oil drain bolt on the crankcase with its gasket.
steps.title: Remove the crankcase drain bolt

steps.instruction: Remove the engine oil drain bolt on the oil tank with its gasket.
steps.title: Remove the oil tank drain bolt

branches.condition: Large flakes or chunks: do not refill and ride; have the engine inspected and record it.
branches.label: Metal in the oil

steps.instruction: Let all the oil drain from both the oil tank and the crankcase. Look for metal flakes in the oil and on the bolts.
steps.title: Drain the oil

steps.instruction: Remove the oil filter element cover and pull out the old oil filter element.
steps.title: Remove the filter

steps.instruction: Fit a new O-ring to the oil filter element cover.
steps.title: Fit a new cover O-ring

steps.instruction: Fit the new oil filter element and refit the cover. Tighten the cover bolts to 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft).
steps.title: Fit the new filter

steps.instruction: Fit the oil tank drain bolt with a new gasket. Tighten it to 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft).
steps.title: Refit the oil tank drain bolt

steps.instruction: Fit the crankcase drain bolt with a new gasket. Tighten it to 20 N·m (15 lb·ft).
steps.title: Refit the crankcase drain bolt

steps.instruction: Pour 0.96 L (1.01 US qt) of SAE 10W-40, 10W-50, 15W-40, 20W-40 or 20W-50 four-stroke oil rated API SG or higher and JASO MA (Yamalube is the named brand) into the filler hole. Do not use oil graded CD or higher or oil labelled ENERGY CONSERVING II, and add no additives: the oil also lubricates the clutch.
steps.title: Fill with oil

steps.instruction: Refit the oil filler cap with a new O-ring.
steps.title: Refit the filler cap

steps.instruction: Start the engine and warm it up for ten minutes until the oil reaches about 60 °C (140 °F), then turn it off.
steps.title: Warm to temperature

steps.instruction: With the bike upright, start the engine, wait ten seconds, turn it off and wait a few minutes.
steps.title: Settle the oil

steps.instruction: Read the oil check window: the level must be between the lower edge of the window (minimum) and the maximum level mark. Below the minimum: add the same oil.
steps.title: Read the level

steps.instruction: Start the engine, warm it up for several minutes, turn it off, wait a few minutes and read the level again.
steps.title: Check it again

branches.condition: Turn the engine off immediately so it cannot seize; have the oil system, passages and pump checked and record it.
branches.label: Level does not drop

steps.instruction: Start the engine and let it idle, without revving. Watch the oil level check window: the oil must flow and the level must drop. If the level does not drop, turn the engine off immediately.
steps.title: Check the oil pressure

steps.instruction: Turn the engine off.
steps.title: Stop the engine

steps.instruction: Look round the drain bolts, the filter cover and the filler cap for leaks.
steps.title: Check for leaks

steps.instruction: Write down the date, hours, oil used, amount and that the filter was changed.
steps.title: Record the job

title: Clean and oil the air filter
entry_state: Bike cool, on a stand.
exit_state: Clean, evenly oiled filter sealed in the airbox, covers refitted, recorded.
completeness: Covers access, removal, washing, oiling, greasing the seal and refitting.

required_parts.name: Spare air filter element
required_parts.purpose: Fit if the old one is damaged.

critical_stop_conditions: Never wash the element in gasoline.
Never run the engine without the element fitted.
Filter not sealing all round: do not start the engine.

steps.instruction: Clean and oil the air filter after break-in, then every race (about 2.5 hours); replace it as required. Write down the date and hours.
steps.title: Record the starting point

steps.instruction: Put your fingers under the edge of the fuel tank cap cover and lift it with both hands toward the rear of the bike.
steps.title: Remove the fuel tank cap cover

steps.instruction: Loosen the quick fastener screw of the air filter case cover.
steps.title: Loosen the quick fastener

steps.instruction: Free the two ribs on the cover from the projections on the air scoops and slide the cover forward to remove it.
steps.title: Remove the airbox cover

steps.instruction: Turn the plates on the air filter case to their open position.
steps.title: Turn the plates

steps.instruction: Remove the air filter guide with the element.
steps.title: Take out the filter

steps.instruction: Take the element off the air filter guide, then take the guide and the seal off the element.
steps.title: Separate the parts

steps.instruction: Wash the element in air filter cleaner or kerosene, then squeeze it and dry it completely. Never use gasoline or an acid or alkaline volatile oil. Do not twist it.
steps.title: Wash the element

branches.condition: Fit a new element and oil it the same way.
branches.label: Element damaged

steps.instruction: Look for tears or damage. Damaged: fit a new element.
steps.title: Check the element

steps.instruction: Apply 30 cm³ of Yamaha foam air filter oil or another quality foam filter oil and squeeze out the excess: wet but not dripping.
steps.title: Oil the element

steps.instruction: Fit the seal and the guide to the element, then the element to the air filter guide.
steps.title: Reassemble the element

steps.instruction: Apply lithium-soap-based grease to the whole seal lip.
steps.title: Grease the seal

steps.instruction: Fit the filter so the two projections at the rear of the air filter guide go fully into the two slots in the air filter case. The element must turn up between the guide and the case with no gap: if there is a gap, refit it.
steps.title: Fit the filter

steps.instruction: Turn the plates back to their original position.
steps.title: Turn the plates back

steps.instruction: Fit the two rear slots of the cover over the two edges on the air filter case, line up the ribs with the projections on the air scoops and fit the cover with the fuel tank breather hose.
steps.title: Refit the airbox cover

steps.instruction: Place the bands fully under the seat and refit the fuel tank cap cover.
steps.title: Refit the cap cover

steps.instruction: Write down the date, hours, filter condition and whether a new element went in.
steps.title: Record the job

title: Check or replace the spark plug
entry_state: Engine cold, bike on a stand.
exit_state: Correct plug at the right gap and torque, bodywork refitted, recorded.
completeness: Covers bodywork and tank access, plug removal, reading, gapping, torque and refitting.

required_tools.name: Spark plug cleaner or wire brush

required_parts.name: Spark plug NGK LMAR9E-J
required_parts.purpose: Replacement plug.

prerequisites: No flames or sparks near the fuel tank.
critical_stop_conditions: Plug will not start by hand: stop and check the thread.

steps.instruction: Check the spark plug electrodes after break-in, then every third race (about 7.5 hours); replace it as required. Write down the date and hours.
steps.title: Record the starting point

steps.instruction: Remove the seat.
steps.title: Remove the seat

steps.instruction: Remove the left and right air scoops.
steps.title: Remove the air scoops

steps.instruction: Unbolt the fuel tank, turn it 180° clockwise and set it in the frame. Do not pull hard on the fuel hose.
steps.title: Move the fuel tank
verification: Tank out of the way, hose not strained.

steps.instruction: Remove the holder over the plug cap.
steps.title: Remove the holder

steps.instruction: Clean away the dirt round the spark plug so nothing can fall into the cylinder.
steps.title: Clean round the plug

steps.instruction: Pull off the spark plug cap.
steps.title: Remove the plug cap

steps.instruction: Unscrew and remove the spark plug.
steps.title: Remove the plug

steps.instruction: The plug must be an NGK LMAR9E-J. Wrong type: replace it.
steps.title: Check the plug type

branches.condition: Use a new NGK LMAR9E-J.
branches.label: Plug worn or wrong

steps.instruction: Damaged or worn electrode: replace the plug. Insulator should be medium to light tan; an abnormal colour means replace it.
steps.title: Read the plug

steps.instruction: Clean the plug with a spark plug cleaner or a wire brush.
steps.title: Clean the plug

steps.instruction: Measure the gap: 0.6–0.7 mm (0.024–0.028 in). Out of range: adjust it.
steps.title: Check the gap

steps.instruction: Clean the plug and gasket surface, screw it in by hand, then tighten it to 13 N·m (9.6 lb·ft).
steps.title: Fit the plug

steps.instruction: Push the plug cap on fully.
steps.title: Refit the plug cap

steps.instruction: Refit the holder.
steps.title: Refit the holder

steps.instruction: Put the fuel tank back in place and bolt it down.
steps.title: Refit the fuel tank

steps.instruction: Refit both air scoops.
steps.title: Refit the air scoops

steps.instruction: Refit the seat.
steps.title: Refit the seat

steps.instruction: Write down the plug reading, the gap and whether a new plug went in.
steps.title: Record the job

title: Check and adjust the clutch lever free play
entry_state: Bike on a stand, engine stopped.
exit_state: Free play in range, locknuts tight, recorded.
completeness: Covers the free play check and adjustment at the lever and at the cable.
critical_stop_conditions: Clutch slips or will not free: do not ride.

steps.instruction: Inspect and adjust the clutch after break-in, then every race (about 2.5 hours). Write down the date and hours.
steps.title: Record the starting point

branches.condition: Go to the test.
branches.label: Free play correct

steps.instruction: Measure the free play at the end of the clutch lever before the cable starts to work the clutch: 7.0–12.0 mm (0.28–0.47 in).
steps.title: Check the free play

branches.condition: Use the adjuster on the cable.
branches.label: Not enough adjustment

steps.instruction: Turn the adjuster at the lever until the free play is correct.
steps.title: Adjust at the lever

steps.instruction: Slide back the clutch cable cover.
steps.title: Slide back the cable cover

steps.instruction: Loosen the locknut on the cable adjuster.
steps.title: Loosen the cable locknut

steps.instruction: Turn the cable adjuster until the free play is correct.
steps.title: Adjust at the cable

steps.instruction: Tighten the locknut to 4.3 N·m (3.2 lb·ft).
steps.title: Tighten the locknut

steps.instruction: Return the clutch cable cover to its place.
steps.title: Refit the cable cover

steps.instruction: Start the engine and check the clutch does not slip and frees fully.
steps.title: Test the clutch

steps.instruction: Write down the free play and anything you adjusted.
steps.title: Record the job

title: Check the hydraulic clutch fluid and lever
entry_state: Bike on a stand, engine stopped.
exit_state: Fluid level checked, no leaks, lever set, recorded.
completeness: Covers the fluid level against the baseline, leak check and lever position.

required_parts.name: Clutch fluid DOT 4
required_parts.purpose: Only if topping up, same type as in the system.

critical_stop_conditions: Clutch fluid strips paint and plastic: wipe spills at once.
Spongy lever: do not ride until the clutch is bled.

steps.instruction: Check for clutch fluid leaks after break-in, then every race (about 2.5 hours); check the clutch fluid level every 45 hours; replace the clutch fluid every four years. Write down the date and hours.
steps.title: Record the starting point

steps.instruction: Put the bike on a stand on level ground so the top of the clutch reservoir is horizontal.
steps.title: Level the bike

branches.condition: Find the leak first. Add only DOT 4 fluid of the type already in the system, set the level to the baseline, and bleed the clutch if the level was very low.
branches.label: Below the baseline

steps.instruction: Compare the clutch fluid with the baseline in the reservoir. Above the baseline: the friction plates are wearing, have the clutch checked. Below the baseline: look for a leak in the hydraulic clutch system.
steps.title: Read the fluid level

steps.instruction: Look round the master cylinder, hose and release cylinder for fluid.
steps.title: Look for leaks

steps.instruction: While pushing the clutch lever forward, turn the lever adjusting bolt until the lever sits where you want it. Tighten the locknut to 5 N·m (3.7 lb·ft).
steps.title: Set the lever position

steps.instruction: Pull the lever: it must feel firm and the clutch must free and engage smoothly.
steps.title: Test the clutch

steps.instruction: Write down the fluid level and anything you adjusted.
steps.title: Record the job

title: Check, adjust and lubricate the drive chain
entry_state: Bike on a stand, engine stopped.
exit_state: Slack in range, wheel aligned, axle torqued, chain lubricated, recorded.
completeness: Covers measuring, adjusting with alignment, torque and lubrication.
prerequisites: Engine stopped; keep fingers away from the sprockets.
critical_stop_conditions: Chain too tight overloads the engine; too loose can skip and damage the swingarm.
Damaged chain or hooked sprocket teeth: replace before riding.

steps.instruction: Clean, lubricate and check the slack and alignment of the drive chain after break-in, then every race (about 2.5 hours). Write down the date and hours.
steps.title: Record the starting point

steps.instruction: Raise the rear wheel off the ground with a maintenance stand and make sure the bike cannot fall.
steps.title: Lift the rear wheel

steps.instruction: Shift the transmission into neutral.
steps.title: Select neutral

steps.instruction: Pull the chain up above the chain guide mounting bolt with a force of about 50 N (5.0 kgf, 37 lbf).
steps.title: Pull the chain up

branches.condition: Go to lubrication.
branches.label: Slack in range

steps.instruction: Measure between the chain guide and the bottom of the chain. It must be 50.0–60.0 mm (1.97–2.36 in) with the bike on the maintenance stand.
steps.title: Measure the slack

steps.instruction: Loosen the rear wheel axle nut.
steps.title: Loosen the axle nut

steps.instruction: Loosen both chain puller locknuts.
steps.title: Loosen the locknuts

steps.instruction: Turn both adjusting bolts by the same amount until the slack is right, so the wheel stays aligned.
steps.title: Set the slack

steps.instruction: Push the rear wheel forward so there is no gap between the swingarm end plates and the swingarm ends.
steps.title: Push the wheel forward
verification: No gap at the end plates.

steps.instruction: Tighten the rear wheel axle nut to 135 N·m (100 lb·ft).
steps.title: Tighten the axle nut

steps.instruction: Tighten the chain puller locknuts to 21 N·m (15 lb·ft).
steps.title: Tighten the locknuts

steps.instruction: Measure the slack again the same way.
steps.title: Recheck the slack

steps.instruction: Clean the chain and lubricate it with chain lube.
steps.title: Clean and lubricate the chain

steps.instruction: Write down the slack before and after and the chain condition.
steps.title: Record the job

title: Check the brakes: lever, pedal, fluid, pads and hoses
entry_state: Bike on a stand, engine stopped.
exit_state: Brakes checked and set, recorded.
completeness: Covers lever and pedal position, fluid level, pads, hoses and a function test.

required_parts.name: Brake fluid DOT 4
required_parts.purpose: Only if topping up, same type as in the system.

critical_stop_conditions: Spongy lever or pedal: do not ride.
Brake fluid damages paint and plastic: wipe spills at once.

steps.instruction: Adjust the lever and pedal, check the fluid level and leaks after break-in, then every race (about 2.5 hours); replace the brake fluid every year. Write down the date and hours.
steps.title: Record the starting point

branches.condition: Go to the pedal.
branches.label: Position right

steps.instruction: There must be no free play at the brake lever end. The standard lever position is 100 mm (3.94 in), adjustable within 86–105 mm (3.39–4.13 in).
steps.title: Check the lever position

steps.instruction: Remove the brake lever cover.
steps.title: Remove the lever cover

steps.instruction: Loosen the locknut, turn the adjusting bolt to the position you want and tighten the locknut to 5 N·m (3.7 lb·ft).
steps.title: Adjust the lever

steps.instruction: Refit the brake lever cover.
steps.title: Refit the lever cover

steps.instruction: Check the brake pedal position: 0.0 mm (0.00 in) from the top of the footrest to the top of the pedal. To adjust, loosen the locknut, turn the adjuster and tighten the locknut to 6 N·m (4.4 lb·ft).
steps.title: Check the pedal position

steps.instruction: Stand the bike upright with each reservoir top horizontal. Fluid at or below the lower level mark: add DOT 4 of the same type already in the system, keeping water out.
steps.title: Check the fluid levels

branches.condition: Replace the pads before riding and record it.
branches.label: Pads worn

steps.instruction: Apply the brake and look at each pad. Front pads: replace them as a set when the wear indicator grooves have almost disappeared. Rear pads: replace them as a set when the wear indicator grooves have almost disappeared.
steps.title: Check the pads

steps.instruction: Look for cracks, damage or wear on both brake hoses. Check the front hose clamp is tight and the rear hose holder is tight. Hold the bike upright, apply each brake several times and look for leaks.
steps.title: Check the hoses

branches.condition: Air in the system: do not ride; have it bled and record it.
branches.label: Soft or spongy

steps.instruction: On a dry surface, use the front and rear brakes separately and check each works properly with no drag.
steps.title: Test the brakes

steps.instruction: Write down the fluid levels, pad condition and anything you adjusted.
steps.title: Record the job

title: Do the pre-ride check
entry_state: Bike on a stand, engine cold.
exit_state: Every pre-ride item checked, faults fixed or recorded.
completeness: Covers the daily check of fluids, controls, brakes, chain, wheels, steering, suspension and fasteners.
prerequisites: A few minutes before every ride.
critical_stop_conditions: Throttle that does not snap shut: do not start the engine.
Spongy brakes or a fuel leak: do not ride.

steps.instruction: Write down the date and hours before the ride.
steps.title: Record the date

steps.instruction: Check the coolant is filled up to the radiator cap (engine cold) and the cooling system does not leak.
steps.title: Coolant

steps.instruction: Check the tank holds fresh gasoline and the fuel line does not leak.
steps.title: Fuel

steps.instruction: Check the engine oil level is correct and the crankcase and oil lines do not leak.
steps.title: Oil

steps.instruction: Check the gears shift correctly in order and the clutch works smoothly.
steps.title: Gears and clutch

steps.instruction: Check the throttle grip works and its free play is right; lubricate the grip and housing if needed.
steps.title: Throttle

steps.instruction: Check the front brake play and that both brakes work.
steps.title: Brakes

steps.instruction: Check the chain slack and alignment and that the chain is lubricated.
steps.title: Drive chain

steps.instruction: Check for wear, set both tyres cold to 100 kPa (15 psi), check no spokes are loose and the wheels have no play.
steps.title: Wheels and tyres

steps.instruction: Turn the bars: smooth, with no play.
steps.title: Steering

steps.instruction: Check the fork and shock move smoothly with no oil leaks.
steps.title: Fork and shock

steps.instruction: Check the clutch and throttle cables move smoothly and are not caught when the bars turn or the fork moves.
steps.title: Cables

steps.instruction: Check the exhaust pipe is tightly mounted and not cracked.
steps.title: Exhaust

steps.instruction: Check the rear sprocket bolts are not loose.
steps.title: Rear sprocket

steps.instruction: Check moving parts work smoothly; lubricate where needed.
steps.title: Lubrication

steps.instruction: Check the chassis and engine for loose bolts and nuts.
steps.title: Bolts and nuts

steps.instruction: Check the stator coil, ECU and ignition coil connectors are tight.
steps.title: Connectors

steps.instruction: Check the bike is set up for the track and weather and all maintenance is done.
steps.title: Settings

steps.instruction: Write down anything you adjusted or that needs attention.
steps.title: Record the job

title: Wash the bike and do the after-wash check
entry_state: Bike back from riding, engine stopped.
exit_state: Clean, dry, lubricated bike, recorded.
completeness: Covers protecting the openings, washing, drying, chain care and lubrication.
critical_stop_conditions: Water inside the airbox: dry it and service the filter before starting.
Brakes not biting after the wash: dry them before riding fast.

steps.instruction: Write down the date and hours.
steps.title: Record the date

steps.instruction: Make sure the bike has cooled down completely.
steps.title: Let it cool

steps.instruction: Block or cover the air duct, the drain hole on the right of the cylinder head, the hole under the water pump housing and the muffler outlet.
steps.title: Block the openings

steps.instruction: Make sure all caps, covers and electrical connectors, including the spark plug cap, are tightly fitted.
steps.title: Check caps and connectors

steps.instruction: Remove stubborn dirt such as burnt-on oil with degreaser and a brush, keeping it off seals, gaskets, sprockets, the chain and wheel axles. Rinse it off with water.
steps.title: Remove stubborn dirt

steps.instruction: Wash with warm water, mild detergent and a soft clean sponge, then rinse well. Do not aim a pressure washer or hose jet at wheel or swingarm bearings, fork or brake seals, electrical parts, the muffler, hoses or the air intake, and do not wash with the seat or covers removed.
steps.title: Wash

steps.instruction: Dry the bike with a chamois or absorbent cloth.
steps.title: Dry

steps.instruction: Dry the chain straight away and lubricate it so it does not rust.
steps.title: Dry and lube the chain

steps.instruction: Apply corrosion protection spray to metal surfaces, keeping oil and wax off the brakes, tyres, rubber and plastic.
steps.title: Protect metal

steps.instruction: Make sure there is no oil or wax on the brakes or tyres; clean the discs and pads with brake cleaner or acetone if needed. Test the brakes before riding fast.
steps.title: Check brakes and tyres

steps.instruction: Take the covers off all the openings you blocked.
steps.title: Unblock the openings

steps.instruction: Lubricate the cables, the brake and clutch lever pivots and the pedal pivots.
steps.title: Lubricate

steps.instruction: Write down anything you found that needs attention.
steps.title: Record the job
